title.narrative: Ethiopian Seed Partnership plus (ESP+)

description.narrative: ESP+ aims to reach and work with the following organisations and individuals: domestic seed companies, seed businesses, seed producer cooperatives, seed banks, the Ethiopian Seed Association (ESA), young men and women entrepreneurs and graduates, prospective students and mid-career professionals for short courses. ESP+ also targets working with 2 universities, international NGOs, humanitarian organisations, international seed companies and men and women farmers. ESP+ will support an enabling environment through relevant government organisations.

The mission of the Ethiopian Seed Partnership plus (ESP+) is to increase small-scale food producers’ food security, nutrition, and resilience to shocks and stresses by improving access to quality seed of adapted varieties. ESP+ builds upon the Ethiopia-Netherlands Seed Partnership by reaching beyond its original mandate to enable the business of the private sector and enters new areas affected by drought and conflict. Here, we strengthen humanitarian responses to seed insecurity, build capacities in farmer- & community-based seed systems and rehabilitate seed service delivery where it has collapsed. ESP+ aims to deliver farming men and women high quality seed much needed for food security and nutrition, and climate resilience. ESP+ will increase farming households’ crop productivity and diversity, create jobs and increase the area under sustainable agricultural practices.

To work towards achieving the mission of ESP+ and achieve the impact, the partnership is targeting four primary outcomes: (1) Private sector strengthened in its contribution to food, nutrition and climate resilience; (2) Uptake of innovations and empowerment of young men and women increased; (3) Effective seed insecurity response, and (4) Enabling transformation. To achieve the first primary outcome, ESP+ aims to contribute to intermediary outcomes ESP+ works in four components, each corresponding with a primary outcome. The component on private sector development works through doubling and diversifying seed production; organizing private sector; and improving the performance of value chains for nutrition. The component on innovations and empowerment works through improving the performance of selected knowledge institutes; enrolling young men and women in internships; and increasing the uptake of sustainable agricultural practices. The new component of effective seed insecurity response focuses on conflict, disaster and climate related shocks and stresses and aims at strengthening farmer and community based seed systems and humanitarian efforts to become more fit for purpose. For the enabling transformation component, ESP+ works through leveraging trade and investment in the seed sector; enhancing the provision of seed regulatory services; identifying and promoting solutions to systemic problems; and convening the humanitarian, development and peace (HDP) nexus to align efforts.
